reader.requirement: At 85, when an EXIT PROGRAM in the same program executes within a PERFORM range, the statements control then reaches (the caller's, after its CALL) are not part of that range. The called program returns and, per §1985:X.5.4.4 GR2, every PERFORM it executed is considered ended, so a later CALL meets no stale return. An EXIT PROGRAM in a program that was not called continues with the next statement (X.5.4.4 GR1) and stays in the range.

reader.edition-search: CallEmitter#EmitExitProgram has no edition reference: it tests __asCalled and throws ProgramReturn, which unwinds every nested dispatch frame. DispatchEmitter.cs and ControlFlowEmitter.cs were grepped as for GR11.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: gr12.cob prints the same at 85 and 2023; 2023 adds only the COBOL0903 warning.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the listed witness (pb3491) exercises GO TO, not EXIT PROGRAM. It does not exercise EXIT PROGRAM inside a PERFORM range of a called program, nested PERFORMs ended by one EXIT PROGRAM, a second CALL after such an exit, or EXIT PROGRAM in the run unit's first program (probed below).

reader.notes: EXIT PROGRAM in a called program throws ProgramReturn, which unwinds every PERFORM's dispatch frame. The caller's statements therefore never join the range, and a later CALL starts with no active PERFORM. In a program that was not called, EXIT PROGRAM does nothing and the range completes. All probes printed the expected lines at 85.
